newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Motors plans to export cars in mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Motors plans to export cars in mid-1998.

text.p: Samsung Motors Inc, a unit of South Korea's Samsung Group, plans to export cars from mid-1998 to mostly emerging markets, a company official said on Monday.
He said about 20,000 to 30,000 units would be exported by the end of 1998 out of a total of 80,000 units the company was expected to produce during the year.
Samsung Motors said last year its car production would start from March in 1998 in its Shinho plant in Pusan built with a total investment of two trillion won.
The official said shipments would be made mainly to Southeast Asian nations and the Middle East.
"But we will also tap markets in the U.S., European Union and Japan," he said.
Samsung Motors plans to increase its annual output capacity to 500,000 units in 2002 and one million by 2010, he said.
The Samsung Group won a government licence to build cars in a technical tie-up with Japan's Nissan Motor Co Ltd in 1994 to enter South Korea's already crowded automobile industry.
Samsung Motor, set up by the group the following year, began construction of its Shinho plant in April 1995.
